trypsinization abolishes Ca2+ regulation of PTH secretion, without affecting Ca2+ entry into the cytosol.

trypsinization abolished Ca2+-regulation of PTH secretion, without affecting Ca2+-dependent Ca2i+ changes, indicating that Ca2+-regulated PTH secretion is mediated by a Ca2+sensor on the cell surface.

In summary, our research is concerned with
the mechanism of Ca2+-regulated hormone release from parathyroid cells, with particular emphasis on a Ca2+ receptor on the cell surface.
the role of the calcium sensor in the control of hormone secretion.
the regulation of the parathyroid hormone.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
Ca2+ does not regulate PTH secretion via a Ca2+-sensing receptor on the cell surface of the parathyroid cells.
trypsinized parathyroid cells are not capable of Ca2+-regulated secretion, but the Ca2+ sensor is not on the surface of the cell.
trypsinization abolishes Ca2e+-regulated PTH release by destroying the Ca2+-sensor mechanism.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the Ca2+-regulated secretion of PTH is controlled by a Ca2+ receptor on the plasma membrane of parathyroid gland cells.
the Ca2+ sensor for PTH secretion in the parathyroid cells resides in the cell membrane and is trypsin-sensitive, but not Ca2+ sensitive.
Ca2+-regulated secretion of PTH is mediated via a surface Ca2+ sensor that is destroyed by trypsinization.
The main takeaway from our work is that
a Ca2+-sensor on the surface of bovine paracryoid cells is involved in the regulation of PTH secretion by Ca2e+.
a Ca2+-sensing receptor on the surface of bovine parthyroid cells is required for Ca2+-regulated secretion of parathy-roid hormone (PTH).
Ca2+ is not a direct trigger for PTH secretion.
